newsitem.title: GERMANY: Body of kidnapped German businessman identified.
newsitem.headline: Body of kidnapped German businessman identified.

text.p: A body found in woodland outside Frankfurt on Saturday has been identified as that of a German multi-millionaire kidnapped more than two weeks ago, police said on Sunday.

The identification was little more than a formality after police said on Saturday they were almost certain the body was that of Jakub Fiszman and clothes found on the corpse matched a description of what Fiszman was wearing when he was abducted.
A brief police statement said genetic tests had now established the identity definitively.
The search for Fiszman had gripped Germany for days, involving hundreds of police, sniffer dogs and even Tornado reconnaissance jets.
Fiszman, 40, whose family fortune has been put at over 400 million marks ($250 million) but who kept out of the public eye, was abducted outside his office in Frankfurt on October 1.
Two suspects, Rainer Koerppen, 48, and his son Sven, 26, have been in custody since Wednesday.
Prosecutors said on Friday the son had confessed to helping with the kidnap and that he and his father had taken Fiszman to the woodland area a few days after his abduction.
Police were able to narrow down the search area after Sven Koerppen gave them more information on Friday night.
Fiszman's brother Georg paid a ransom of four million marks ($2.6 million) on October 10, but the kidnappers reneged on an agreement and failed to free him the following day.
Police have recovered most of the ransom from the garden of an apartment in Wiesbaden owned by Rainer Koerppen's parents.
The last sign that Fiszman was alive came the day after his kidnap, when he made a telephone call to a friend.
